title: Provider faces — a simulator receives a command, confirms it, and drives its feedback contact
description: The inverted side of the HAL contracts, with nothing paired to it. serviceProviderSet drives SetDigitalOutput INTO the DeviceSimBlock's IDigitalOutputProvider — legal because the provider handler declares that inbound — and the block reacts: it records the command, confirms back what it applied on the same contract, and drives its IDigitalInputProvider feedback contact. serviceProviderExpect asserts both outbounds. The analog pair runs the same loop, so all four trios are exercised. Then the take-up knob is switched off and the same command arrives again: the simulator records it and deliberately does nothing, so the last confirmation and the feedback contact stay where they were — hardware that ignored a command, modelled as block behaviour rather than host magic. Everything runs stepped, so the whole loop is deterministic.
